svg.text: Simulated devices — the FIRE CONTROL UNIT's aiming: lock, lead, ranged line, guidance switch, view (SD-S4d, DESIGN_Simulated_Devices §3.13g)
Full colour = SPECIFIED by this mockup · grey dashed + 'unchanged' = CONTEXT, not specified · the picture, the targets and the wall are world effects, illustrative.
specified HUD element (full colour, dark halo — the station's HudText over the view)
Frames are 640 × 360 (16:9). Panels 27, 31, 32: the sight head's own line of sight (SightMode = Slaved, D-181); 28 – 30: the missile unit's sight, then the round's seeker view. Layout is PROPOSAL.
the type lists which exist · LOCK:

Every chip is a HudPanel button (D-122) with its hotkey badge (D-124 — proposals); a switch is the latching panel element of D-142 (a click or its hotkey steps it; beside a replica the replica's rotary owns it, D-135).
The aim chips (TRACK, RANGE) sit in a row above the command chips so the six commands of panels 20-23 keep their place.
27 · RWS CONSOLE, TRACKING a crossing truck — lock box, LEAD, GUN (dv-rws-lock)
Scope: the lock box on the target, the LEAD pipper (where the muscle is aiming the round, ahead of the truck), the GUN
marker (the barrel, still turning), RANGE, the MODE and RNG switches, the TRACK chip set.
the gun follows the LEAD · FIRE held fires on target
the TRACKING box (green corners) with its label `TGT n · range` · the LEAD pipper (cyan diamond,
dotted from the target's middle): the aim point the MUSCLE is using now (`WeaponTaskStatus.AimPoint`,
D-175) — ahead of the truck by the lead · the GUN marker: the barrel's replicated pose, still turning
toward the LEAD · the lamp SLEWING (amber) until the gun is on the LEAD, then READY · RANGE with its
mode word · the MODE and RNG switches · the TRACK chip set (lock held)
the compass · the unit lines · the picture and the truck (world)
The cross is the SLAVED sight head's line of sight (D-181): while locked it rides the target, so the operator needs no stick.
The LEAD pipper is the muscle's, read from the weapon's turret part by the console's tick (a declared read) — the device
never calculates it. TRACK again breaks the lock (the box ends LOST, then the cross is the stick's again).
PROPOSAL: the cyan of the LEAD, the dotted line, the box label, the SLEWING relabel, the RNG switch's place and the
28 · LOCK-ON MISSILE UNIT, LOCKED before launch — seeker sight, GUIDE ▸ SEEKER (dv-lock-fire)
Scope: the unit's own sight with the lock box on the tank, the lock's range, GUIDE on SEEKER, READY, the TRACK chip
set. No MODE switch: a launcher offers SINGLE only (D-157).
FIRE launches · the seeker holds the lock
the TRACKING box (green) · the lock's range · GUIDE on SEEKER (the round flies at the locked target,
D-176) · READY only with a lock when the type requires one · TRACK set · no MODE switch (a launcher
fires SINGLE) · VIEW greyed: no round is flying
the compass · the unit lines · the picture and the tank (world)
The lock is the DEVICE's tracker holding `FireControl.Target` (D-174); the missile's own seeker (its cone,
`GuidedRound.SeekerCos`) takes over at launch. A type with no lock requirement shows READY without it. GUIDE's positions
come from the type: a Javelin-class unit offers SEEKER and STICK, a wire-guided box STICK alone (greyed), a TOW-class
PROPOSAL: the lock label, the range row and the switch's place are mine.
29 · IN FLIGHT, NO LOCK — the missile's view, GUIDE ▸ STICK offered (dv-lock-lost)
Scope: the missile's view (VIEW ▸ MISSILE) with the seeker ring, the lost lock, NO LOCK in amber where READY was,
GUIDE on SEEKER with STICK pressable, TRACK pressable.
GUIDE ▸ STICK flies it · TRACK a new target
VIEW set, labelled MISSILE (rocket glyph) · the seeker ring · the LOST box on the target outside it · the
GUIDING chip (red) · LOCK / FLIGHT lines · NO LOCK (amber lamp and message) · GUIDE on SEEKER
with the STICK position pressable and TRACK pressable (the round has a link, D-176) · FIRE and ARM
the compass · the picture (the chase view of the round, world) and the tank
The unit leaves READY for NO LOCK when `GuidedFlight.State` becomes NoLock (D-177): the seeker no longer sees its
target; the round flies on to where it last saw it. A round with no link would show the same lamp and offer nothing: GUIDE and
TRACK greyed. When the flight ends the unit sets the view back to its sight by itself (D-178).
PROPOSAL: the ring's radius, the LOST box and the amber lamp are mine; the design names NO LOCK, not its look.
30 · RETARGET IN FLIGHT — GUIDE ▸ STICK, TRACK on the new target B (dv-retarget-in-flight)
Scope: the missile's view with the stick gauge, GUIDE on STICK, the old target A lost, the new target B locked
(TRACKING), the hint to hand the round back to the seeker.
GUIDE ▸ SEEKER sends the round at B
GUIDE set to STICK with the hand-over hint · the stick gauge (axes 0 / 1) · the lamp STICK (gold: the
operator flies it) · A's lost box · B's TRACKING box and range · TRACK set (a new lock, `TargetSeq`
moved) · the round is flown by the stick until GUIDE ▸ SEEKER
the compass · the picture and the two tanks (world)
TRACK works in the missile's view (D-178): the tracker holds B while the stick keeps the round on a course that keeps B in the
seeker's picture. GUIDE ▸ SEEKER then re-targets the round (D-176): its `Target` becomes B and the seeker takes over;
PROPOSAL: the hand-over hint, the gauge's place and the gold lamp are mine.
31 · RWS CONSOLE, UNLOCKED — the cross on a parked truck, AUTO range (dv-rws-point)
Scope: the slaved sight's cross, the GUN marker lagging behind it, RANGE measured under the cross (AUTO), RNG on
AUTO, the TRACK and RANGE chips, the lamp.
READY when the GUN marker reaches the cross
the cross (the sight's own line) · the GUN marker offset from it while the barrel turns · RANGE measured
under the cross every tick with its mode word (AUTO) · the RNG switch on AUTO, RANGE chip greyed
(nothing to latch) · TRACK pressable (a lock instead of the cross) · the SLEWING lamp and message
the compass · the unit lines · the picture and the truck (world)
The gun follows the POINT at the measured range under the cross (`AimMode = LINE`, D-181), laid from the barrel's own
place so the sight-to-barrel offset is solved; the GUN marker shows the lag the drives add. The round flies straight (no drop
term for a direct round today, D-181 ③), so the super-elevation is zero; an arc weapon's comes from the range automatically.
PROPOSAL: the range row's wording and the marker's place are mine.
32 · RWS CONSOLE, RANGE HELD — lased at 600 m, the cross on a nearer wall (dv-rws-range-hold)
Scope: RNG on HOLD, the held range (amber) beside the live range under the cross, RANGE pressable (re-lase), the aim
RANGE re-lases at the cross · RNG ▸ AUTO follows it
RNG on HOLD · RANGE with its HELD word in amber (the latched value) · the live range under the cross in
grey beside it · RANGE pressable (a new lase replaces the held value) · READY: the aim at the held range is
the compass · the unit lines · the picture and the wall (world)
The weapon aims at the point 600 m along the cross (`RangeM` latched from `WeaponTaskStatus.MeasuredRange`, D-181 ④),
not at the wall: the cross moves the aim along the same range, as a stored-range fire-control computer does. A unit never
ranged uses the type's zero range. Pause freezes the latched value with the lay (D-83).
PROPOSAL: the amber HELD word and the UNDER CROSS line are mine.
